subject: Control-plane residency assurance and short-lived analytics hops
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.z@medisphere.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: David Liu <dpo@medisphere.com>
Date: 2027-02-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick clarification: control-plane metadata & short-lived analytics hops

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for taking this. We're moving through procurement for a pilot and two final items came up from our privacy team that we'd like written answers to before we sign the SOW: 

1) Control-plane metadata: does any customer-identifying control-plane metadata (user IDs, tenant IDs, request timestamps tied to customer IDs) ever leave the EU as part of normal operation (for routing, telemetry, or triage)? We need a clear statement of whether metadata is stored/processed outside the EU.

2) Transient analytics/telemetry hops: we've seen architectures where aggregated telemetry or analytics pipelines briefly process traces or aggregated metrics in the US for analytics. For our use case (healthcare PII-light), we need to know whether you ever route telemetry or aggregated logs outside the EU, even for short windows, and if so what the maximum expected window is and what subprocessors are involved.

3) Evidence request: can you provide an example audit-log snippet (sanitized is fine) showing timestamps and region tags for a sample request? Also a current subprocessor roster with regions.

If you can confirm the answers in writing (and note where the control plane sits), that will speed legal review. If it helps, happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Security & Privacy
Medisphere Health

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.z@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-08T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: control-plane metadata & short-lived analytics hops

Alice — thanks, and really appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front, longer notes below and a proposed next step. I've attached a one-page residency summary and our latest subprocessor roster.

Summary (short):
- Customer payloads (requests/responses, embeddings, generated tokens) can be pinned to EU and we will not egress permanent copies outside the EU region when pinning is requested.
- Control-plane metadata (tenancy IDs, routing tags) is stored in our control-plane service; by default the control plane for EU customers is in the EU control-plane cluster. We do run a global control plane for certain hosted customers, but for enterprise EU-region-only deployments we provide a customer-dedicated control-plane instance in the EU.
- Telemetry/analytics: default hosted telemetry aggregation can be processed in the US for cross-tenant analytics. For customers requiring EU-only processing we can route telemetry aggregation to EU-only pipelines or provide an option to exclude specific telemetry types. For transient failover scenarios we support temporary short-lived hops with notice; typical window we propose is up to 72 hours for failover/incident triage.

Attachments included: residency-summary-2027.pdf, subprocessor-roster-Feb2027.csv (see column B: region).

Longer notes / clarifications:
- Payload custody: when you select "region pinning: EU" at activation we ensure all persisted payloads are written to EU storage backends only. Ephemeral caches (in-memory GPU KV cache) are located in the serving region. No persistent backups are copied to non-EU storage.

- Control-plane detail: the control plane stores tenancy mappings, rate-limit counters, and non-content metadata used to route requests. For our dedicated/private deployments we instantiate the control plane inside the customer's VPC/region. For hosted pilots we can enable EU-dedicated control plane instances (this is the default for customers on an enterprise plan).

- Telemetry and analytics: we have two telemetry paths: (1) per-customer operational logs (audit logs, request traces) and (2) aggregated metrics for product telemetry. Operational logs tied to customer IDs are retained in-region if you request regional custody. Aggregated metrics are de-identified and historically have been processed in the US; however, we can now configure aggregated metrics to be processed only in EU clusters on request.

- Temporary hops: we offer a documented temporary-hop playbook (we'll attach a draft if useful) that sets the max window, notification cadence, and required approvals for any cross-region processing.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min sync? I'll loop Marissa from Legal and Kim from Privacy on the thread so they can confirm DPA language and the temporary-hop addendum.

Thanks — Elliot
Elliot Price
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: residency-summary-2027.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
Attachment: subprocessor-roster-Feb2027.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.z@medisphere.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: control-plane metadata & short-lived analytics hops

Hi Alice — thanks Elliot. A few legal/contracting clarifications to put on the table so procurement knows what to expect: 

- DPA addendum: we can provide an addendum that codifies region pinning for customer data, control-plane placement for enterprise plans, and a temporary cross-region processing clause limited to incident response and failover. We'll propose language that limits any temporary cross-border processing to a maximum continuous window of 72 hours unless renewed by written approval.

- Audit/evidence: we can provide sanitized audit log exports and a one-off operational snapshot showing region tags (we'll redact user identifiers for the sample). That will be part of the evidence package for onboarding.

- Subprocessors: the roster attached in Elliot's email is current; key US subprocessors used for analytics are listed in the CSV. If you require EU-only subprocessors, we can discuss a migration sequence or escrow for analytics (this would be a commercial & operations conversation).

Proposed process to close: 
1) Redwood provides: (a) sanitized audit-log snippet, (b) DPA addendum draft w/ 72-hour temporary-hop clause, (c) DocuSign envelope of DPA addendum.
2) Medisphere legal reviews and either counters or accepts.
3) If EU-only telemetry is required, Marissa (legal) + Kim (privacy) will coordinate a scoping call to estimate timelines and potential cost/impact.

I'll add the DPA addendum draft to DocuSign and link it in the thread, and I'll upload the sanitized log sample once I have ops scrub it.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice.z@medisphere.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: David Liu <dpo@medisphere.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: control-plane metadata & short-lived analytics hops

Marissa / Elliot — thanks for the detail and the concrete next steps. Two quick asks before we sign: 

1) Audit snippet: can you attach the sanitized audit snippet in this thread (we need to show it to our DPO). Ideally it shows at least request timestamp, region tag, and action (GET/POST).
2) KMS residency: confirm whether customer-managed keys (BYOK) can be provisioned in a EU KMS and whether Redwood will ensure key material never leaves the EU. If not possible, please explain the constraints.

If both look good we'll proceed to DocuSign review. If you can include estimated turnaround for the EU-only telemetry option (ballpark days/weeks), that would help procurement budget.

Thanks,
Alice
